section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section introduces the verse and raises several textual difficulties regarding the plural language, the mention of Moshe writing, the repetition, and the eternal relevance of the journeys.
section.t: "These are the journeys of the children of Israel who went out of the land of Egypt etc. And Moshe wrote their goings out according to their journeys etc. And these are their journeys according to their goings out."
And the precise points
in this are known,
that it says "These are the journeys,"
which is in the plural,
and it concludes "who went out of the land of Egypt," which is only the first departure and journey.
Also, it is not understood why it says "And Moshe wrote,"
for Moshe Rabbeinu wrote the entire Torah,
so what does this inform us?
Also, what is the repetition of "their goings out according to their journeys" and "their journeys according to their goings out,"
and the reversal of order from the beginning to the end.
And in general, one must understand,
what is the relevance of the narrative and knowledge of the order of the journeys,
and even for that generation, the Midrash explains
a parable of a king and his son who traveled etc., when they returned they counted all the journeys and events within them,
but the Torah is eternal,
and therefore this narrative is relevant in all times and in all places.
And therefore, this narrative pertains to all times and all places.
